result: Found the cause of the stop-after-N-profiles: it is not a counter, a limit or a timeout. growApplicantList() calls assertRunnable() on every pass, which throws hiddenPageError the moment the tab is hidden or while state.wentHidden is still latched from an earlier switch (only beginRun clears it). That call sat outside the row loop's try/catch, so the throw was not a pause - it propagated out of extractAllApplicants and runEveryApplicant rethrew it, killing the run; noteReturnToTab then restarted it from the first row, which is the stop-and-start-over the recruiter sees. N was simply however many rows were already rendered before the list first needed growing. Growing the list is now inside the same pause handling extractApplicant has had since 3.7.7: wait for the page, clear the latch, continue where it left off. Stop still ends the run and a non-pause error still surfaces. waitForVisibleAgain's five-minute bound is the only limit, so nothing can spin.
